title: Two-phase commit across orders and payments
description: An order and its payment live in two different databases. Commit both or neither using two-phase commit.

problemStatement.overview:
Placing an order writes a row to the orders database and a charge to the payments database. If one commits and the other doesn't, you either ship for free or charge for nothing.

Two-phase commit (2PC) makes the pair atomic. A coordinator asks every participant whether it can commit, records a single decision, and then tells everyone the outcome. The trick is the point of no return: once a participant votes yes, it has promised to commit if told to.

The outline is on the board. Fill the blocks. Traps break atomicity or make recovery impossible.
problemStatement.yourTask: Order the steps of a two-phase commit, from starting the transaction to participants releasing their locks.
yourTaskSteps: Fill each empty block from Unused.
hints: There are two promises: the participant's yes vote, and the coordinator's decision.
The decision has to survive a coordinator crash.
Once the decision is made, it cannot be taken back. Only delivered.
problemStatement.moat:
Setter notes, not shown to learners.

Required chain: global-txid → send-prepare → durable-yes → log-decision → send-commit → commit-release.
Optional splice: ask-outcome on send-commit → commit-release.
Five traps.

platformSpec.passMessage: Atomic across both databases: prepare, durable votes, logged decision, commit.

pieces.title: Start a global transaction
pieces.blurb: The coordinator assigns a global transaction ID. order-processor writes to both databases under that ID.

pieces.title: Coordinator sends prepare
pieces.blurb: When the application is ready to commit, the coordinator asks every participant: can you commit?

pieces.title: Participants persist, then vote yes
pieces.blurb: Each participant writes its changes and a prepare record to disk, holds its locks, and votes yes. It can no longer abort on its own.

pieces.title: Coordinator logs the commit decision
pieces.blurb: With yes votes from every participant, the coordinator writes 'commit' to its own durable log. This is the commit point.

pieces.title: Send commit to every participant
pieces.blurb: The coordinator tells each participant to commit, retrying indefinitely until each one acknowledges.

pieces.title: In-doubt participant asks for the outcome
pieces.blurb: If the commit message is slow to arrive, a participant that voted yes can ask the coordinator what was decided. It still may not decide alone.

pieces.title: Participants commit and release locks
pieces.blurb: Each participant makes the changes visible, releases its locks, and acknowledges to the coordinator.

pieces.title: Commit on the first yes vote
pieces.blurb: As soon as one participant votes yes, the coordinator decides commit to save time.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Commit requires a yes from every participant. One no means abort.

pieces.title: Prepared participant aborts on timeout
pieces.blurb: If the coordinator goes quiet for too long, a participant that voted yes rolls back to free its locks.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: After voting yes, a participant gave up the right to abort. The coordinator may already have decided commit.

pieces.title: Skip the coordinator's log
pieces.blurb: The votes already show everyone agreed, so the coordinator doesn't need to write the decision down.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: If the coordinator crashes without a logged decision, in-doubt participants can never learn the outcome.

pieces.title: Others commit when one votes no
pieces.blurb: If payments votes no, orders still commits its part and payments retries later.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: That breaks atomicity. One no vote aborts the transaction everywhere.

pieces.title: This is two-phase locking
pieces.blurb: 2PC is another name for 2PL: acquire all locks in phase one, release them in phase two.
pieces.trapIfPlaced: Different ideas. 2PL gives serializable isolation on one database; 2PC gives atomic commit across many.
